title: Chicken Croquetas with Creamy Béchamel
summary: Crisp, golden croquetas with a soft, creamy centre of béchamel and finely shredded poached chicken, fried in panko and served hot with lemon.
equipment: large heavy pot or deep fryer

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
lemon, cut into wedges, to serve

steps.title: Poach
steps.text: Put the chicken and bay leaf in a small pan, cover with cold water by 2 cm, bring to a bare simmer and cook for 12-15 minutes, until the thickest part reads 74 °C. Lift out and cool for 10 minutes; gentle heat keeps the breast moist.

steps.title: Shred
steps.text: Pull the chicken into very fine shreds with your fingers, then chop briefly so no piece is longer than 1 cm. Large pieces make the croquetas hard to roll and prone to splitting.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Heat the milk in the rinsed pan until steaming, then keep it hot off the heat. Hot milk blends into the roux without lumps.

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a heavy saucepan over medium-low heat, add the onion and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until very soft and pale.

steps.title: Roux
steps.text: Add the chicken and the flour and stir for 2 minutes, until the flour coats everything and smells toasty, not raw.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Whisk in the hot milk a ladle at a time, letting it thicken between additions, then cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring with a spoon, until it is a thick paste that pulls away from the pan. Season with the salt, pepper and nutmeg. It should be much stiffer than a sauce.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Spread the mixture in a shallow dish, press cling film onto the surface and chill for at least 6 hours, until firm. Overnight is even better: a fully cold base is far easier to shape.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: With damp hands, roll heaped tablespoons (about 30 g) into 5 cm logs, to make about 24.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Roll each log in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on, and set them on a lined tray. Chill for 30 minutes so the coating sets and stays on in the oil.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil to 180 °C. Fry 5-6 at a time for 2-3 minutes, turning, until deep golden and the centre reads 74 °C. Drain on paper towels and serve hot with lemon.

tips: If the mixture is too soft to roll after chilling, it was not cooked long enough; return it to the pan and cook for a few minutes more.
Check the oil between batches; below 170 °C the croquetas absorb oil and may burst.
Any gaps in the crumb let the filling leak, so coat each one fully.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Fried croquetas are best eaten straight away. Coated, unfried croquetas freeze for 2 months on a tray, then in a bag. Fried leftovers keep for 2 days in the fridge; reheat at 200 °C for 8-10 minutes, until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
